answer: Identity is an enclave ticket, not a key. To speak in a round an agent must spend a fixed serial chain of hashes over its signing key, and each hardware enclave may hold only one ticket at a time, so a thousand voices mean a thousand chips or a thousand sequential chains. A bridge contract admits a ticket once and rejects repeats, so nothing is recycled across pools. A sudden gale of registrations only lengthens the queue; it adds no weight. Honest agents burn minutes of idle compute, and each ticket is a lotus that opens once per epoch from its own stem, never from a cutting.
